stemBlocks.value: A rectangle has length (x + 8) cm and width (x − 3) cm, and an area of 70 cm². Calculate the value(s) of x.
Think first: Read the two side expressions from the diagram, multiply them, and set the product equal to 70.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p107-q16 from workbook page 107.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the area equation from the diagram.
Apply the quadratic formula with a = 1, b = 5, c = −94.
Evaluate and reject the root that gives a negative width.

contentBlocks.value: x ≈ 7.51 or x ≈ −12.51; the latter makes x − 3 negative

strategyBlocks.value: Form (x + 8)(x − 3) = 70, rearrange to standard form, solve with the quadratic formula and keep only the root that gives positive sides.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: x = (−5 + √401)/2 ≈ 7.51 (2 d.p.); the root x ≈ −12.51 is rejected because it would give negative side lengths.

whyThisWorks.value: The diagram supplies the two linear side expressions and the question supplies their product, which is exactly enough information to pin down x. Expanding turns the geometric statement into a quadratic equation, and the formula solves it whether or not the numbers are friendly. The physical constraint that both x + 8 and x − 3 must be positive eliminates one of the two mathematical roots.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the perimeter formula because the diagram shows a rectangle.

examTip.value: Label the diagram with which expression is length and which is width before writing any equation — mislabelling is easy under time pressure.
